artist: Hermann Lungkwitz (1813-1891) - German-Texan landscape painter, part of the community of German immigrant artists (with Richard Petri and Carl von Iwonski) who settled near Fredericksburg/New Braunfels/Austin in the 1850s and documented the Hill Country region in watercolor and drawing.
category_basis: All works date 1848-1885 and depict Hill Country locations (Austin's Shoal Creek and Barton Creek, the Guadalupe and Colorado Rivers, Fredericksburg-area mills and ranches). Lungkwitz died in 1891; life+70 expired 1961, and most of these works also predate 1929 outright. Every file is tagged PD-old-100-expired / CC-PD-Mark on Wikimedia Commons.
note: Searched Portal to Texas History (texashistory.unt.edu) and Library of Congress directly per instructions; did not find additional verifiably public-domain Hill Country sketches there distinct from what Wikimedia Commons already aggregates from the Witte Museum / Museum of Fine Arts Houston / Texas institutions holding Lungkwitz's work. All images below are sourced via Wikimedia Commons, which itself cites the originating Texas museums.
